name: Partnerships, alliances and business development pursuits
one_line: The organizational situation of PURSUING a commercial relationship that does not exist yet - a prospect, a partner, an alliance, a reseller, a piece of new work being bid for. The organizing anchor is the PURSUIT: one named counterparty, one opportunity, tracked from first contact through pitch and proposal to signature or loss. That is what separates it from customer account management, which begins after the deal is won, and from sourcing, which is the same documents seen from the buying side of the table. Absorbs the legacy row ops.partnerships-bd. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognizes the situation and writes NO field rows, because the business_operations schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

an outbound proposal structure: a document addressed TO a named external organisation carrying an understanding-of-your-needs section, a proposed approach, a commercial section and a validity period. Addressed-outward plus a validity period together is the shape.

a pipeline structure: a spreadsheet or export whose header row names an opportunity, a counterparty, a stage, a value and an expected close date, with one row per pursuit. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a pre-contractual instrument structure: a non-disclosure agreement, a memorandum of understanding, a letter of intent or a term sheet - documents that exist ONLY in the pursuit stage and disappear once a contract is signed.
a partner-programme structure: tiering criteria, a partner application form, a referral or margin schedule, and a joint go-to-market annex.
a pitch-deck structure aimed outward: a problem framing for a named counterparty, credentials and case studies, a proposed commercial model, and a next-steps slide.

a bid or qualification structure that answers somebody else's numbered questions - a completed pre-qualification questionnaire, a filled-in pricing schedule, a method statement responding to a solicitation reference issued by another organisation.
a CRM export: a machine-generated filename with a date token, and a header row naming account, contact, stage, owner and last activity.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

the direction of the relationship, which is the central judgement of this row: whether a named counterparty is a prospect being pursued, an existing customer being served, a supplier being bought from, or an employer being applied to. A company name and a proposal decide none of it. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
the side of the table on a bid: the same specification, pricing schedule and clarification log exist in the buyer's sourcing file and in this row, and only purpose distinguishes them.

separating a pursuit that is still a pursuit from one that has closed - the moment a proposal becomes a signed contract, ownership moves to contract administration or account management, and the file itself often does not change.
an unheaded deck or one-pager with a counterparty logo and no framing.

a purpose-coherent pursuit pack whose members are individually unremarkable - an NDA, a deck, a pricing sheet, three case studies and a meeting note. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
never_alone: an external organisation's name alone. This is the tempting false file for this row and the reason it needs care: a folder of company-named PDFs is as likely to be suppliers, customers, employers or news as prospects. Read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”
the word proposal, partnership, pitch or deck in a filename alone - a proposal is also a research grant application and an academic project proposal.
an NDA alone. Non-disclosure agreements are signed for recruitment, diligence, procurement, disputes and consulting, and the document is near-identical in all of them.
a contact name or a business card alone - 00 treats contact data as privacy-side rather than as a source of folder proposals.

an extension or a source_type alone - 00: “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”
a bare 4-digit number read as a year, a deal value or an opportunity number.

membership in a download session that dropped a counterparty's whole document set at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

work_types: prospect or partner profile and qualification note
letter of intent, memorandum of understanding or term sheet
partner programme application or agreement draft
meeting and call notes from the pursuit
case study or reference material used in the pitch
grouping_reasons: one pursuit: the NDA, the deck, the proposal, the pricing and the notes for one counterparty and one opportunity, held together by purpose rather than by content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one proposal across its drafts and its sent version, which is a version family before it is anything else.

one counterparty across several pursuits over years, which is a real reason to group and the one most likely to tempt a customer or partner status onto a file that merely names the company. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one partner programme across its applicants, which is a group of pursuits rather than a single pursuit.
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single NDA with no pursuit around it is a standalone record.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: business_operations declares no field rows (J-IND / PR-6, D1's deferral as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15), so no dimension can branch - a dimension naming an undeclared field opens a tree level no fact could ever fill. Held as prose for the pass that may license fields: the natural anchor is the organisation, then the COUNTERPARTY, then the pursuit or opportunity, then the document function. This is one of the few rows in the family where a counterparty level genuinely belongs above the work, because the relationship outlasts any single pursuit and because that is how sales and partnership teams actually file - but it also means the tree records who an organisation has been talking to, which is exactly the disclosure the row's sensitivity note is about. “The recommendation should follow the practical rule that a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” - a pricing sheet is meaningless without knowing which counterparty and which opportunity it was built for. Not time-first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - a pursuit that runs across a year boundary must not split in two. The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this later; this is a recommendation, not a frozen filesystem.

collides_with.signal: The same counterparty, the same deck template and often the same folder, separated only by whether the deal has closed. The discriminating evidence: a proposal with a validity period, a pipeline stage, or a pre-contractual instrument supports this row; an account identifier, delivered-service reporting, adoption metrics and a renewal date supports account management. Provenance: inference.

The mirror-image problem: a bid response, a pricing schedule and a clarification log exist identically on both sides of one competition. The discriminating evidence: possession of the evaluation apparatus - several suppliers' responses, scoring matrices, an award to issue - supports the sourcing row; a single organisation's own outbound response, win themes and internal pricing approval supports this row. Provenance: inference.

NDAs, letters of intent and term sheets are pursuit artifacts and live contractual instruments at the same time, and the signed proposal becomes the contract. The discriminating evidence: executed signature blocks, an obligations register, notice and renewal dates support contract administration; the pursuit that preceded signature supports this row. Provenance: inference.

For an individual or a very small firm, business development and consulting engagement are one continuous activity with the same documents. The discriminating evidence: a delivered engagement with a scope, deliverables and timesheets supports the career row; an unwon pursuit with a proposal and a validity period supports this row. Provenance: inference.

A freelancer's proposal, credentials pack and NDA are nearly indistinguishable from a job application, a portfolio and an employment NDA. The discriminating evidence: an application to a named role, a job reference, or an interview cycle supports the career row; an offer to perform work for a fee supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Partner enablement and joint go-to-market annexes are produced by both situations and share the same decks. The discriminating evidence: a launch date, positioning and readiness checks supports go-to-market; a named counterparty being pursued supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Approaching a funder is business development with different vocabulary: a case for support is a pitch, a grant application is a proposal, and a donor pipeline is a pipeline. The discriminating evidence: a funder, a charitable purpose, a grant reference or a restricted-fund framing supports the nonprofit row; a commercial counterparty and a fee supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Term sheets, heads of terms and redlined drafts circulate during a pursuit and inside a legal negotiation file, and are literally the same documents. The discriminating evidence: a matter reference, a client identifier, privilege markings or counsel involvement supports the law-practice row; a commercial pursuit run by the parties themselves supports this row. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The home for a standalone NDA, proposal or partner agreement with no accepted pursuit group around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The cautious outcome for a counterparty-named deck or an introduction email whose relationship direction is unresolved - the commonest ambiguity in this row. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The correct home for a pipeline export, a contact export or a commercial offer with no accepted group - files that disclose who an organisation is talking to and on what terms. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The safe outcome for a password-protected pursuit pack or an unreadable counterparty document. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

The home for a counterparty's own marketing material and public reports saved during qualification, which are reading material rather than pursuit artifacts. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

sensitivity_why: A pursuit file discloses two things that are damaging in different directions: what an organisation is willing to charge or concede, and who it is talking to. A pipeline export is the second of those at scale - every prospect, every value, every probability in one file - and a contact export is a list of named individuals at other organisations with their direct numbers. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and private correspondence and contact material sit inside it, with 00 treating contact data as privacy-protected rather than as a source of folder proposals. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Whether an individual's own pursuit of work belongs here or in career. For a company, business development and job-seeking are unmistakably different activities; for a freelancer, a consultant or a sole trader they are one activity with two vocabularies, and the same proposal PDF is a bid on Monday and a job application on Tuesday. Putting a person's freelance pitches under a business-operations branch, or their company's proposals under a career branch, would both be wrong for somebody. The row does not resolve it because the answer depends on whether the user files as an organisation or as a person, which is exactly the kind of default about someone's real life that a catalogue must not pick.
